sources.citation: Jolkesky, Marcelo Pinho de Valhery. 2016. Estudo arqueo-ecolinguístico das terras tropicais sul-americanas. Tese de doutorado, Universidade de Brasília. 846 pp.
sources.note: No phonology content for Yumana: the language appears only as ~30 cited forms in cognate/loan sets (e.g. YMN jama 'cachorro', YMN wataragaon 'aracuã', YMN/PSE zenemo 'camaleão') and in one sentence on subgroup geography. Full PDF (56 MB) downloaded, a full-text search for stress/accent (yumana|YMN|jumana), extract kept, PDF deleted.
sources.venue: Tese de doutorado, Universidade de Brasília. 846 pp

sources.citation: Adelaar, Willem F.H. & Hélène B. Brijnen. 2014. Johann Natterer and the Amazonian languages / Johann Natterer e as línguas da Amazônia. Revista Brasileira de Linguística Antropológica 6(2): 333-352. DOI 10.26512/rbla.v6i2.16285.
sources.note: No phonology of Jumana. The article surveys Natterer's 72 language samples; Jumana is only named in the inventory of Arawak languages (p. 336). The section on Natterer's orthographic notation (pp. 339-340) discusses his diacritics generically: in Bororo the acute on é marks a central vowel, elsewhere a mid front vowel, 'the motivation behind these different uses of é is not clear'; hiatus/spaces mark glottal interruption. Cabixí 'may have been tonal judging from.. the diacritics'. Nothing links any diacritic to stress in the Schumana list.

sources.citation: Loukotka, Cestmir. 1968. Classification of South American Indian languages (ed. Johannes Wilbert). Los Angeles: Latin American Center, UCLA. 453 pp. Arawak stock, 'v. Languages of the Jumana group', p. 138 (+ comparative table pp. 138-139).
sources.note: Nothing. Classification entry with location and source, then a 12-gloss comparative table (head, eye, hand, water, fire, sun, house, tapir, maize, one, two, three) with Jumana forms n-ula, un-lo, no-gabi, uhu, oye, somanlu, pana, zema, irari, aphla, liagua, maba?agua (accents as printed: sömanlú etc.); no remark on stress, accent or tone anywhere in the Arawak-stock pages (a full-text search for stress/accent lines 8300-8600 for stress/accent/tone/penult: zero).

sources.citation: Nicolai, Renato (comp.). n.d. 'Vocabulário jumana (Jumana/Jumána/Jumâna)', site Línguas Indígenas Brasileiras — five words 'citado por SCHULLER, Rodolph R., in Revista Americana, 1911. Gr. Equatorial - Arawake - Maipure'.

sources.citation: Schuller, Rodolpho R. 1911. Las lenguas indigenas de la Cuenca del Amazonas y del Orinoco. Revista Americana (Rio de Janeiro) tomo V, fasc. III: 622-661; tomo VI, fasc. I: 25-84. (102-page scan with scanned by Renato Nicolai, Biblioteca Digital Curt Nimuendaju.)
sources.note: Nothing. The only Jumana content is the classificatory sentence 'El vocabulario Jumana, apuntado por Spix-Martius en las cercanias del Rio Yapura, es nu-aruaque' (Rev. Americana VI p. 45 = p. 63) plus a few Martius forms cited in comparative footnotes (e.g. 'aitana, arbol, Jumana', p. 52; 'Cf. Jumana: simia; sol', later); extracted text of all 102 pages has no acento/tonica/prosodia vocabulary at all (one false hit 'adejacentes').
sources.venue: Revista Americana (Rio de Janeiro) tomo V, fasc

sources.citation: Martius, C. F. Ph. von. 1867. Beiträge.. I: Zur Ethnographie. Leipzig: Fleischer. 'Die Jumanas' pp. 483-486.
sources.note: Nothing; ethnography only, language said to be related to Manao and Baré with Tupi/Quechua admixture.

sources.citation: Martius, Carl Friedrich Phil. von. 1867. Beiträge zur Ethnographie und Sprachenkunde Amerika's zumal Brasiliens. II: Wörtersammlung brasilianischer Sprachen / Glossaria linguarum brasiliensium. Leipzig: Fleischer. 'Jumana' pp. 250-252.
sources.note: Nothing. Latin-glossed wordlist (Martius at Maripi, Spix at Caiçara) with sporadic acute accents on forms; footnote p.250 only names the collectors and notes affinities to Moxa, Maypure, Marauha. General orthography note (pp. 28-30, written for Tupi) says the acute 'dient, den Vocal zu schärfen oder die Sylbe zu betonen' — a transcription convention, not a stress rule for Jumana.
